b: Asmodee’s huge-selling co-operative card game Take Time has added to its string of 2026 awards by scooping the Flemish Gouden Ludo family game of the year prize.

Alexi Piovesan and Julien Prothière’s design has now won both of this year’s Dutch-language board game awards, having picked up the Nederlandse Spellenprijs last month, as well as the Swiss Gamers Award and Austrian game of the year prize.

The Gouden Ludo win marks the fourth year in a row that a game has done the double in Dutch-language awards, following the success of SETI last year, Forest Shuffle in 2024 and Wandering Towers in 2023.
That awards recognition follows massive sales numbers for the title, which Asmodee told BoardGameWire in September had sold more than 325,000 copies in less than a year.
Game line manager Auguste Lecoeur said at the time that Take Time’s ‘recommended’ nod in this year’s Spiel des Jahres had been followed by demand for a 30,000-copy reprint from Germany alone.
Take Time fought off competition from fellow Asmodee title Toy Battle and Yoann Levet design Got Five! to win the Gouden Ludo.
This year’s awards featured the introduction of a hobby game category between the long-standing family and expert game prizes, which were introduced in 2016.

Last year’s Spiel des Jahres winner Bomb Busters became the first game to win the new award, having been up against Reiner Knizia design Rebirth, published in Dutch by DSV Games, and Reed Ambrose’s design Wispwood, published by White Goblin.

Hisashi Hayashi’s co-operative bomb defusal game also won the Nederlandse Spellenprijs family game award in 2025, but fell into this year’s eligibility window for the Gouden Ludo due to the timing of its release.
The win marks the third Gouden Ludo in as many years for veteran Dutch publisher 999 Games, which triumphed with The White Castle in 2024 and Sky Team last year.
Bomb Busters, the inaugural winner of the Gouden Ludo’s ‘hobby game’ category
The expert game prize, meanwhile, went to Germán P Millán’s ancient Egypt-themed eurogame Men-Nefer, securing a debut Gouden Ludo for Dutch publisher Keep Exploring Games.
The publisher was in contention for the same prize last year with Unconscious Mind, which ultimately lost out to SETI.
Men-Nefer beat competition from Mathias Wigge’s Ark Nova follow-up Sanctuary and Nestore Mangone’s Stupor Mundi to take this year’s expert game award.
The Gouden Ludo has been awarded every year since 2009, when Matt Leacock’s Pandemic became the first game to take home the prize.

Entries must be Dutch-language games readily available on the Flemish market, with a jury whittling down publishers’ submissions to a shortlist which is then voted on by members of the Forum Federation and Flemish games clubs.
This year’s winners were announced on November 20 ahead of the annual Spel games fair at Antwerp Expo.
